title: I am trying to restore a backed up profile for use in thunderbird.
creator: texiii
content: I was attempting to use Thunderbird Restore Tool to merge multiple Thunderbird profiles. Before I started, I copied the existing Thunderbird profile to a safe location where it has remained undisturbed. The Thunderbird Restore Tool did not produce the desired results, but that is a story for another day. I tried copying the saved profile back to C:\User\Tom Hayden\AppData\Roaming\Thunderbird\Profiles. I then started Thunderbird. It returned something very close to "Your profile file is inaccessible or corrupted". After some research, I edited the profiles.ini to point to the old profile file. Thunderbird would not start. I tried multiple iterations of thunderbird - p to run the profile manager. I was, eventually, able to get thunderbird to start and read the most recent e-mails from the server. However, it would not load any of the old e-mails from the old profile. I went to the profile thunderbird is currently using. Under ...\thunderbird\profile\pd785tbj.Default_User\Mail I found Local Folders-1 and pop3.airmail.net. Under pop3.airmail.net I can see the directory structure I used for my old e-mail. Everything appears to be present and in place. No matter what I do, Thunderbird will not read/load those e-mails. There is also an ImapMail directory with mail.airmail.net. Under it is a directory structure that appears to be what is actually showing up in Thunderbird. How do I restore/reload/recover/whatever the old e-mails in pop3.airmail.net? Please make your answer as explicit as possible.

title: INCOMING EMAILS TAKING A LOT OF TIME TO OPEN AND READ
creator: venkateshkasturi
content:
Hello Folks,

We are a team of around 15 users who have been using Mozilla Thunderbird with Google IMAP for the last few years. Until recently, Thunderbird has been working reliably without any major issues.

However, for approximately the last one week, we have been facing a serious performance issue with incoming emails. Around 12 out of 15 users are experiencing the same problem.

The main issues we are facing are:

Newly received emails take a very long time to download. After clicking on a newly received email, it takes a considerable amount of time to open and display the content. Emails appear to be downloading extremely slowly, even though our internet connection is a 100 Mbps ILL (Internet Leased Line). The issue is affecting multiple users simultaneously, so it does not appear to be limited to a particular user's Thunderbird profile or PC. We have already tried Repair Folder / Repair Inbox, but the issue persists. We are using Google's IMAP servers for our email accounts.

We are currently using Mozilla Thunderbird 153.0.3 (64-bit) – Meadow Badge.

Could this be a known issue or bug in the latest Thunderbird 153.0.3 update, particularly with Google IMAP?

We would appreciate any guidance from the Thunderbird community/support team on how to troubleshoot and resolve this issue. If there are any recommended settings, logs, diagnostics, or Thunderbird configuration changes that we should check, please let us know.

Since this issue is affecting 12 out of 15 users, it is becoming a significant operational problem for our team.

Any help or suggestions would be highly appreciated.

Thank you.
